s: Neural network that converts text, images, or structured data into fixed-length dense vector representations for similarity search.
w: Input (text/image/audio) is tokenized and fed through transformer or specialized encoder layers; the output is a fixed-dimensional vector (e.g., 768-d or 1536-d). Semantically similar inputs produce nearby vectors in embedding space. Models are hosted as APIs or self-hosted containers. Embeddings are pre-computed for documents and stored in vector databases; queries embed in real-time for nearest-neighbor retrieval.
use: RAG retrieval: embedding documents and queries for semantic search
Semantic deduplication of similar content across large corpora
Recommendation engines using embedding similarity between users/items
Classification and clustering tasks via embedding similarity thresholds
avoid: Exact-match keyword search (inverted indexes are faster and cheaper for literal matches)
Tasks requiring structured numeric reasoning (use LLMs or traditional ML instead)
Real-time embedding of massive inputs (video, long documents) without batching

pat.d: Embedding search retrieves context; LLM generates grounded answer.

pits: Model version changes invalidate entire index - version embeddings with model ID, plan re-embedding
Dimension mismatch between indexing and querying models - enforce schema validation
tips: Embedding quality is the foundation of RAG - poor embeddings mean poor retrieval regardless of reranker
Dimension vs quality vs cost triangle: larger dimensions are better but slower to index and search
